desc:
Row n of Pascal's triangle holds the binomial coefficients C(n, 0), C(n, 1), ..., C(n, n). Given n and k, return the sum of the entries C(n, i) for every i with 0 ≤ i ≤ min(k, n), taken modulo 1,000,000,007.

n = 5, k = 2   -> 1 + 5 + 10 = 16
n = 4, k = 10  -> 16   (the whole row)
n = 0, k = 0   -> 1
hints: Each entry C(n, i) can be computed on its own, but recomputing every one from scratch is wasteful. Can you get the entries from a shared table?
Write C(n, i) = n! / (i! (n - i)!). Modulo a prime, division is multiplication by a modular inverse.
Precompute n! and all the inverse factorials once, then add the terms for i from 0 to min(k, n).
editorial: A partial row of Pascal's triangle has no simple closed form, so we add the terms one by one. Each term is n! * inv(i!) * inv((n - i)!), and once the factorials and their inverses are tabulated every term costs O(1).

The modular inverses come from Fermat's little theorem: 1,000,000,007 is prime, so xp-2 is the inverse of x. The inverse factorials can be filled backwards from a single inverse, since inv((i-1)!) = inv(i!) * i.
The running time is O(n + k) and the memory is O(n). As a check, the answer for k ≥ n must be 2<sup>n</sup> modulo the prime.
